title: Create the exception where it is thrown

blocks.text: The stack trace is captured when the exception object is **created**, not where it is thrown, so a pre-built exception kept in a field points at the wrong place in the logs. Write `Connection`:

items: `String send(String message)` returns `"sent: " + message` while the connection is open;

blocks.text: Anyone reading the trace of a failed `send` should be led straight to `send`, every time it fails.

cases.says: An open connection sends; a closed one throws IllegalStateException("Connection closed").
The stack trace's top frame is send, because the exception is created there, not in a field initializer.
Every failed send throws a new exception object with its own trace, never a cached one.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: The stack trace is captured where the exception is created, so it is created at the throw.
